**Major change: Identity handling now fully automated and no longer exposed to users. Skill documentation and workflows reorganized and clarified.**

- User identity (open-id) is now handled automatically by internal scripts—users are never asked for, nor see, any identity information.
- Skill documentation has been restructured for clarity, with updated sections, tables, and stricter rules for identity and data handling scenarios.
- Historical report queries and analysis now always use automated identity handling; forbidden to prompt or expose any identity parameters to end users.
- Removed any user-facing requirements or sample code referencing open-id or user identity values.
- Expanded and clarified documentation on allowed triggers, capabilities, API parameters, and privacy/data security.
- Minor file cleanup and updates to scripts, requirements, and references to support new identity management logic and documentation.

Major refactor and restructuring for improved modularity and compliance.

- Split out common functionality and analysis-specific logic into distinct directories (smyx_common, smyx_analysis).
- Added new modules and scripts for analysis handling, configuration, and API service structure.
- Updated open-id acquisition flow to prioritize reading from config files before prompting the user.
- Expanded, clarified, and enforced stronger rules on open-id validation and cloud-only report queries.
- Removed face_analysis module and associated files to reduce scope and improve maintainability.

- Improved configuration management for API keys and environment selection in shared/common scripts.
- Enhanced config file support for multiple environments (dev/test/prod) with separate YAMLs.
- Refactored utility functions for more robust handling of API credentials and error management.
- Internal code cleanup and better separation of public/private utilities in common modules.
- No change to user-facing core features or skill behavior.

- Updated SKILL.md to add a missing version field in the metadata section.
- No functional changes made; documentation consistency improvement only.

Initial release of Pet Vocal Emotion Analysis Skill.

- Recognizes cat and dog vocalizations from audio/video, inferring emotions (e.g., happiness, anger, anxiety, pain, vigilance) and behavioral intentions (e.g., seeking attention, hunger).
- Requires clear pet sounds and strict open-id acquisition/validation before any analysis or report query.
- Analysis and historical report queries are handled exclusively via a cloud API (no local memory or records used).
- Automatic triggers when users upload pet audio/video or request emotion analysis reports; reports displayed in Markdown tables with direct links.
- Designed for home pet-owner interaction, improving communication and understanding through emotion/intent translation.
